review_reason: RESOLVED after re-fetching the live Gutenberg source directly to check: this excerpt ends immediately after '...our Lives, our Fortunes and our sacred Honor' with no signatories block, and this is CORRECT and COMPLETE, not a truncation. Project Gutenberg eBook #1's own transcriber's note (present in the source, trimmed here along with other boilerplate) explicitly states the transcriber found discrepancies in signer names/placement across source facsimiles and deliberately left the signatures out of this specific edition ('which names I have left out'). So input.txt faithfully and completely reproduces the operative text of this Gutenberg edition -- there is no missing content to add. An earlier verification pass flagged the absence of signatures as an undisclosed gap; re-checking the actual live source resolved this as a non-issue rather than a real defect, and needs_human_review has been set back to false accordingly.

expected_headings.text: THE DECLARATION OF INDEPENDENCE OF THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

expected_no_table_zones.location: the central grievances section (~26 consecutive paragraphs)
expected_no_table_zones.looks_like: a bulleted/numbered list or even a table of short entries
expected_no_table_zones.reason: 26 consecutive short paragraphs almost all begin with the repeated phrase 'He has ...' or 'For ...' (a rhetorical anaphora device), verified directly via grep. This repetitive structural pattern could tempt a structure-inference heuristic into treating each as a list item (reasonable) or, more concerningly, into treating the repeated leading tokens as if they were a column of a table or a set of headings (less reasonable, but a real risk for pattern-matching heuristics that key off repeated line-start tokens). The correct reading is that these are ordinary prose paragraphs forming a single continuous rhetorical list, not a table.

math_notes: No mathematical notation. (Note: contains the date 'July 4, 1776' and enumerable grievances, but no arithmetic/equations.)
notes_for_implementer: This is the deliberately short/minimal-structure fixture (8,218 bytes, 166 lines, exactly ONE heading -- the title). Gutenberg's license boilerplate header/footer was deliberately trimmed since it is not part of 'the document' being tested (it's Gutenberg packaging, not Declaration content) -- this is a curation decision, flagged here for transparency rather than silently done. The main structural interest is the ~26-paragraph anaphoric grievance list ('He has...', 'For...') -- verify Pith treats this as plain prose/paragraphs (optionally recognized as a list), not as a table or as spurious headings, since the repeated sentence-initial tokens are the kind of surface-level pattern a naive heuristic might latch onto incorrectly.
